newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Oct oil trade gap rises 40 pct to $35 mln.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Oct oil trade gap rises 40 pct to $35 mln.

text.p: Peru's oil and derivatives trade deficit was $35 million in October, 40 percent higher than in the same month last year, the Central Reserve Bank said Monday.
The country's oil and derivatives deficit in the first ten months was $269 million, up 12.5 percent from the same period last year, the bank said in its weekly report.

October's imports of oil and derivatives were $70 million, up from $54 million in the same month last year. Exports in October rose to $35 million, up from $30 million in the same month last year, the bank said.
In the first ten months of the year, imports of oil and derivatives rose 27.7 percent to $571 million. Exports rose 45.3 percent to $302 million, compared with the same period in 1995.
Peru's oil deficit swelled 134 percent to $323.2 million in 1995 compared with $138 million the previous year, according to the Energy and Mines Ministry.
